gloss: from the beginning; from the start

definitions.gloss: from the beginning; from the start; from the outset
definitions.explanation: Starting from the very beginning of something. Can indicate either a temporal starting point or that something was the case all along.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めからやり{直|なお}す。
examples.english: To start over from the beginning.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めから{無理|むり}だと{分|わ}かっていた。
examples.english: I knew from the start that it was impossible.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{初|はじ}めから{最後|さいご}まで{目|め}が{離|はな}せなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't take my eyes off this movie from beginning to end.

notes:
A common adverbial phrase combining {初|はじ}め (beginning) with the particle から (from). Used to emphasize that something applies from the very start — whether redoing a task, or expressing that a situation was true all along.

USAGE:
Often implies emphasis or mild frustration — '{初|はじ}めから{言|い}ってよ' (you should have said so from the start). Also used neutrally to describe starting a process from step one.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初|はじ}めからやり{直|なお}す — to redo from scratch
- {初|はじ}めから{終|お}わりまで — from start to finish
- {初|はじ}めから{分|わ}かっていた — knew all along
- {初|はじ}めから{無理|むり}だった — it was impossible from the start

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最初|さいしょ}から — from the very first; slightly more formal and emphatic
- もともと — originally, from the beginning; emphasizes an inherent quality
- {元|もと}から — from the original point; similar to もともと
